title: Logspace membership of the constructed language
statement: Let $f$ be a function on bit strings such that its output length is bounded by a polynomial in the input length, the language of pairs $(x,i)$ for which the $i$th bit of $f(x)$ is true is decidable in logarithmic space, and the language of pairs $(x,i)$ for which $i<|f(x)|$ is decidable in logarithmic space. Let $C,e$ be natural numbers such that $|f(x)|\le C(|x|+1)^e$ for every bit string $x$, and let $m$ be a Boolean mode. Then the language that, on an encoded pair $(z,p)$, tests whether $p$ is below the length of the output associated to $z$ when $m$ is true, and otherwise tests the output bit at position $p$, is decidable in logarithmic space.
hypotheses_covered: The output-bit index language for $f$ is in logarithmic space
The output-length index language for $f$ is in logarithmic space
